rollback_evidence: 1.0.12 wireless wlans, measured on Ruckus R610 Unleashed 200.15.6.212 build 27: the Unleashed CLI has no on-device timer, so Admin returns an unverified change itself in the same run by writing the inverse (compensation), as on FortiADC. A WLAN is created in the unsaved config-wlan context with 'type standard-usage', 'ssid', 'open wpa2 passphrase <generated> algorithm aes', optional 'description' and 'vlan', 'no service' and saved by 'end'; it never broadcasts, because the service is disabled before the save. 'service' and 'no service' switch one WLAN without touching the radios, 'vlan <1-4094>' sets its client VLAN, 'no wlan <name>' deletes it (the answer 'has been deleted' is immediate). The passphrase is generated at the write, held only in memory and not recorded; set the real passphrase of a created WLAN in the Unleashed web interface. Undo of a delete creates the WLAN again with a new generated passphrase, disabled; the old passphrase is not read by Admin and cannot be restored. Only WLANs named in the device entry (wlans) are written; every other WLAN is refused before any write. 1.0.12 wireless dhcp (verification record, measured on the same R610): in the context of the WLAN 'open wpa2|wpa3 passphrase <vault reference> algorithm aes' sets a personal passphrase (the plan holds only the vault entry name WLAN_PSK_*, the privileged transport resolves it), 'dot1x wpa2|wpa3 algorithm AES auth-server name <aaa>' sets enterprise authentication (the listing shows 802.1x-eap and the server), 'acl l2acl|l3acl <name>' / 'no l2acl|l3acl' the ACLs, 'client-isolation isolation-on-ap enable|disable', 'max-clients <1-512>', 'rate-limit perssid_uplink|perssid_downlink <0-500>' and 'rate-limit uplink <n> downlink <n>' / 'no rate-limit' (per client). The inverse writes the previous values; a passphrase cannot be restored (the plan never holds one), so the inverse types a newly generated passphrase the administrator must replace in the web interface. A change to a broadcasting WLAN needs endpoint_impact.
